conversation.Statement: Good morning, this is Officer Mark Davis with the Internal Revenue Service, badge number 307195. Whom am I speaking with today?
Uh, hi, this is Jamie Turner. I got a call saying there was an issue with my taxes?

Yes, Jamie, the reason for my call is regarding discrepancies found in your recent federal tax filings. Our records indicate significant misreporting for the last two years. Have you been notified about this before?
No, this is the first I've heard of it. I just finished college and filed my taxes online. I didn't know there was a problem.

I understand this can be alarming. Unfortunately, our audit team discovered what appears to be underreported income as well as several unclaimed deductions. I need to verify some details with you before we proceed. Can you confirm your current mailing address?
Yeah, it's 124 Oakridge Avenue, Apartment 3B, Silverton.

Thank you, Jamie. As of this morning, a formal case, number IR-675821, is open against you for tax evasion and fraud. I want to help you resolve this before it escalates, but you must follow my instructions carefully.
Wait, tax evasion? That sounds serious. Am I in trouble?

Jamie, right now there is an arrest warrant prepared in your name. If the matter is not resolved today, local authorities will be notified to detain you. However, there is a temporary payment option to suspend legal action while we review your case.
An arrest warrant? I had no idea. I don't want to get arrested! What do I do?

I can initiate the cancellation process, but only if you settle the outstanding balance immediately. The amount due, including penalties, is $3,200. I will provide you with payment instructions to secure your account.
That's a lot of money. I don't have that much just sitting around. Can I pay online or something?

Due to the urgency and nature of the violation, we cannot process traditional online payments. Instead, the IRS now accepts immediate settlements via Bitcoin for rapid resolution. Do you have a cryptocurrency wallet?
No, I don't. I've never used Bitcoin before. I don't know how that works.

That's alright, Jamie. Many people are new to this. All you need to do is visit a nearby pharmacy or major retailer, like CVS or Walmart, and use cash or your debit card to purchase Bitcoin through a CoinFlip or Coinstar kiosk. I can guide you through the process.
Are you sure? I thought the IRS only took checks or something.

This is a newly approved emergency method for high-priority cases like yours. Delays could result in asset seizure or arrest. Please do not hang up while you go to the store. Do you have transportation available right now?
Yeah, I can get there in about ten minutes. What exactly do I need to do when I get to the store?

Once you arrive, locate the Bitcoin kiosk. I will provide you with the IRS settlement wallet address: 1Fz4h4G9Vyx8zY3wKpLqT9K9. Use your funds to purchase the equivalent of $3,200 in Bitcoin and send it to this address. I'll stay on the line to assist.
Okay, but I'm kind of nervous. Will this definitely stop the arrest?

As soon as your payment is received, the warrant will be suspended and your case will be prioritized for review. If you have any trouble with the kiosk, let me know so I can walk you through each step.
Alright. I'm leaving now. Should I call you when I get there or keep you on speaker?
Keep me on speaker so I can ensure there are no issues and confirm your transaction. If anyone at the store asks, simply say it's for a personal purchase, do not mention the IRS to avoid confusion.
Okay, I'll try. I just really hope I'm not in trouble.
As long as you follow my instructions, Jamie, you will not face any further penalties. Please let me know once you arrive at the store.
